ai.title: Unibuc - NLP at "Voight-Kampff" Generative AI Detection PAN 2025
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.16612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes the approach of the Unibuc - NLP team in tackling the "Voight-Kampff" Generative AI Detection task from PAN at CLEF 2025. In the Subtask 1: Voight-Kampff AI Detection Sensitivity we have explored different approaches of leveraging embeddings extracted from LLMs, using either classical ML models or further fine-tuning LLMs with a classification head for the downstream binary classification task. Our experiments showed that using a majority vote ensemble of classical ML models (Light GBM, XGB, Logistic Regression and SVM) is comparable with fine-tuning for downstream task achieving around 99.4% F1 score. For the Subtask 2: Human-AI Collaborative Text Classification we explored a way of combining features at different layers extracted using transformer backbone with layer-wise projection and attentive pooling which proved modest results.
ai.summary: This paper describes the approach of the Unibuc - NLP team in tackling the "Voight-Kampff" Generative AI Detection task from PAN at CLEF 2025.

ai.title: Fine-Grained Generative Hallucination Detection and Correction for Aerial Image Captioning
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.15809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aerial imagery captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) plays a vital role in applications such as surveillance, disaster response, and large-scale environmental monitoring. Automatic generation of textual descriptions for such imagery is essential for reducing manual inspection overhead and enabling better downstream decision-making. However, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), despite their impressive captioning capabilities, are prone to hallucination, producing descriptions that are inconsistent with the visual input. This problem is significantly amplified in aerial imagery due to its unique challenges such as extreme viewpoint variation, small objects, class imbalance, and ambiguous visual entities. Existing hallucination detection approaches either rely on computationally expensive large external models such as GPT-4, which perform poorly on aerial domains, or treat the problem as a rigid binary classification task, ignoring the inherent uncertainty in ambiguous cases. To address these limitations, we propose a lightweight, reference-free framework for hallucination detection and correction in free-form aerial image captioning. Our method leverages state-of-the-art MLLMs, specifically InternVL3 and Qwen2.5-VL, to detect hallucinated content in generated captions with minimal computational overhead. ai.title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.16986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. This paper presents Primer, an open-source, LLM-agnostic AI-supported system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations. Educators contribute their knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students, while generative AI produces responsive variations of practice for students. Primer uses a multi-agent system centered around executing educator's instructional intent through the entire learning experience. We hope that by releasing Primer as an open-source system, including its prompts and GitHub repository, we provide a foundation for development and research on educator-in-the-loop AI authoring, multi-agent educational workflows, and simulation-based pedagogy. Further, by allowing the use of various AI models, including local and open source models, we provide the opportunity for implementation under varied governance regimes. Primer points toward a model of educational AI in which instructors can create locally grounded practice opportunities based on their own materials, goals, examples, and knowledge of students.

ai.title: CoLFA: Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.14980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Failure attribution in multi-agent systems requires tracing error formation to identify the decisive error step and the responsible agent. However, agents' division of work and information exchange lead to Interleaved Steps and Cluttered Content, requiring models to link executions and check details in lengthy records. This makes it difficult to balance localization accuracy and token cost. We find that multi-agent collaboration also leaves records of how executions connect and content passes between them as results are formed, providing evidence for tracing error formation. Based on this observation, we propose CoLFA (Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution), which uses collaboration cues to organize the attribution input according to how results are formed, determining which steps are examined and how their content is presented. Through Handoff-Guided Step Expansion and Cross-Referenced Content Organization, CoLFA helps the model focus on examining error formation and the role of each decision while reducing the processing of irrelevant and repeated records. Across five settings spanning Who&When and LongRCA and three backbone models, CoLFA achieves the highest exact step-localization accuracy with the lowest token consumption. Compared with individual baselines in each setting, CoLFA improves accuracy by up to 37.50% and reduces token consumption by up to 97.6%.
ai.summary: Failure attribution in multi-agent systems requires tracing error formation to identify the decisive error step and the responsible agent.

ai.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.14766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use agents (CUAs), and standard text-prompted LLMs. We find that human behavior is best captured by a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from their timing---and similarly for frontier models. However, unlike humans, none of the tested models seem to efficiently adapt their behaviors to their partners' over the course of the game. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that humans perform implicit probabilistic reasoning about continuous-time signals in dynamic social settings, and that such reasoning mechanisms may emerge without real-time experience. ai.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.14910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment: heterogeneous tasks induce distinct Jacobian geometries, causing their common null space to shrink dramatically and leaving insufficient admissible directions for conflict-free updates. We propose the Conflict Index to quantify this geometric interference, and introduce Mu-Edit, which mitigates multi-task conflicts via (1) conflict-aware ordering to minimize cumulative interference, and (2) dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the null space when ordering alone is insufficient. Experiments across five functional domains and three backbones show that Mu-Edit significantly outperforms existing baselines in multi-task editing performance while preserving general capabilities, and remains effective under incremental task arrival.

ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Naloxone and nalmefene, the two types of opioid overdose reversal medications, are available as both injections and nasal sprays and as generic and brand versions. Naloxone is also available in low and high doses. Low-dose naloxone nasal sprays have been available for over-the-counter (OTC) use since 2023. GAO’s analysis of federal data show that all enrollees of Medicare Part D and Medicaid had coverage of some form of naloxone in 2025 and 2024, respectively, while coverage of nalmefene—a newer and longer acting medication—was less common (see figure). Medicare Part D Enrollee and Medicaid Coverage of Opioid Reversal Medications Note: For the purposes of this report, GAO identified states as having Medicaid coverage if there was utilization of opioid overdose reversal medications; other states may have coverage but no utilization of these medications. For example, for a covered nasal spray that costs $150, enrollees would pay about $38 or $53, depending on whether their coinsurance rate was 25 percent or 35 percent. ai.title: K-12 Education: Data Show That Less than Half of Students Were Ready for Kindergarten in Selected States
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found In general, GAO’s review of 11 studies found that publicly funded preschool programs contribute to children’s readiness for kindergarten in literacy, math, or both. Specifically, 10 studies found positive associations between preschool programs and kindergarten literacy scores, and seven of the studies that assessed math scores also found positive associations with these scores. One study did not find evidence of an effect in either area. These studies also suggest that public preschool programs affect student demographic groups differently. For example, one study found that English learners benefitted more from a public preschool program in Virginia than non-English learners. It also found that children from lower-income families benefited more from attending the program than children from higher-income families. GAO’s analysis of kindergarten entry assessment (KEA) data from five selected states also found a link between preschool, certain demographic factors, and kindergarten readiness. School districts with higher enrollment in public or private preschool were associated with higher kindergarten readiness in three of five selected states, according to GAO’s regression analyses. In addition, higher-poverty school districts were associated with lower readiness in four states. ai.title: Military Personnel: More Complete Data Needed on Humanitarian Reassignments and Safety Transfers
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Humanitarian reassignments and safety transfers are exceptions to the standard relocation process. These transfers may be granted to service members who meet specific criteria. The Department of Defense (DOD) defines humanitarian reassignment as the relocation of a service member to another duty station based on humanitarian factors that include family emergency or other hardship. Safety transfers are relocations for service members or their dependents who are threatened with bodily harm or death, where authorities cannot ensure their safety at their current location. The military services have each developed and implemented their own processes for receiving and adjudicating requests, and each includes common steps. Common Military Service Process for Humanitarian Reassignment According to available military service data, over 15,000 service members requested humanitarian reassignment from fiscal year 2022 through 2025. The Army and the Marine Corps approved at least 95 percent of these requests in each year. Navy and Air Force approval rates ranged from 74 to 84 percent and 66 to 83 percent, respectively. According to available data, documentation, and military service officials, nearly 400 service members requested safety transfers over this period, and the military services approved 87 percent of those requests. trade.title: 經濟部貿易救濟審議會就我對韓國及中國大陸非方向性電磁鋼品反傾銷案與對中國大陸特定鋁箔落日調查案作成產業損害之肯定認定
trade.source_name: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.via: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 經濟部今（9）日召開貿易救濟審議會，會中就我國對韓國及中國大陸冷軋扁軋非方向性電磁鋼品反傾銷案，以及對中國大陸特定鋁箔課徵反傾銷稅屆滿5年之落日調查案等2案之產業損害調查結果進行審議，前者最後認定國內產業遭受實質損害；後者認定國內產業損害可能因停止課徵反傾銷稅而繼續或再發生。 經濟部表示，就電磁鋼品案調查發現，韓國及中國大陸涉案貨物進口量大幅增加且持續降價，自112年起以低於國產品價格銷售，國內產業為維持競爭力被迫跟進減價，惟因減價幅度不及涉案傾銷貨物而流失客戶，導致生產量、產能利用率、內銷量、市場占有率等經濟指標全面下滑，並自113年起內銷出現虧損且逐步擴大。雖然國內產業114年相關經濟指標一度改善，但115年上半年再度轉弱，顯示涉案傾銷貨物進口已對國內產業造成顯著不利影響。 另針對中國大陸特定鋁箔落日調查案，調查發現，課徵反傾銷稅期間涉案貨物進口量雖有減少，但仍以低價與國產品競爭，使得國內產業營運狀況略有好轉後又再度惡化。復考量中國大陸鋁箔產能過剩且出口能力強勁，加上越來越多國家對其鋁箔採行貿易救濟措施或提高關稅，已嚴重限縮其外銷市場。若我國停止課徵反傾銷稅，涉案貨物可能再度低價大量出口至鄰近且其已建立行銷通路的我國市場。在國內需求尚未好轉、產業體質仍然脆弱的情況下，可能使我國特定鋁箔產業之損害繼續或再發生。 經濟部表示，上述2案產業損害認定結果將通知財政部，並由該部提交關稅稅率審議小組審議是否課徵及繼續課徵反傾銷稅。該2案之產業損害調查報告公開版可於今年12月9日起至貿易署網站（網址：https://www.trade.gov.tw/）「經貿往來」/「我國採行之貿易救濟措施」/「案件調查」項下之「調查報告」下載。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：綜合企劃組邱組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7361

trade.title: 進口人無償或減價提供賣方用於生產及銷售進口貨物之物品或勞務，應計入完稅價格申報
trade.source_name: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.via: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 海關近來接獲進口人詢問國外自備模具之費用是否應計入完稅價格等問題，關務署表示，倘進口人有「無償」或「減價」提供賣方用於生產或銷售該進口貨物之物品或勞務，應主動將其計入完稅價格向海關申報，避免因未申報相關費用而須補稅或送查價，影響通關速度。 關務署說明，依據關稅法第29條規定，進口貨物之完稅價格以交易價格為課徵關稅基礎，為確保完稅價格核估之正確性，若進口貨物之實付或應付價格中，未計入下列由買方無償或減價提供賣方用於生產或銷售該貨物之物品及勞務，應將其合理攤計之金額或減價金額計入完稅價格： 一、組成該進口貨物之原材料、零組件及其類似品。 二、生產該進口貨物所需之工具、鑄模、模型及其類似品。 三、生產該進口貨物所消耗之材料。 四、生產該進口貨物在國外之工程、開發、工藝、設計及其類似勞務。 關務署提醒，倘進口人有此類產銷協助費用，應提供買賣合約書、商業發票、付款證明等必要文件供海關審核，若無客觀及可計量之資料，海關將依關稅法第29條第4項規定無法按交易價格核估其完稅價格，籲請進口人注意，避免海關查核時發現短（漏）報，影響自身權益。 新聞稿聯絡人：賴科長 聯絡電話：（02）25505500分機2703

trade.title: 401(k) Plan Investments: DOL Can Take Steps to Prepare for Expected Private Equity Growth
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found Private equity is one type of investment within a broad, undefined category called alternative assets. It differs from publicly traded equity in who can invest in it, how it is valued, and what disclosures are required, among other things. GAO’s review of selected research papers that analyzed private equity investment fund performance found no consensus on the performance of private equity relative to publicly traded equity, which is an important consideration when making investment decisions. GAO found a range of performance findings among research papers we reviewed, as well as ranges in data analyzed, benchmarks for performance comparisons, and methodologies. For example, one group of papers found that private equity funds outperformed publicly traded equity for the sample of funds they analyzed during the specific time-periods studied. The size of the overperformance varied widely. In one paper the benchmarks did not include a risk premium, the excess return that some experts believe a private equity investment should provide to justify higher investment risks. Another group of papers found that private equity funds underperformed publicly traded equity during the time-period studied, accounting for the underlying risk or fees, which can be higher for private equity than for publicly traded equity products.
